races.name: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Fillies Maiden

runners_data.name: Cloughleagh Bridge
runners_data.comment: Beaten well on debut at Leopardstown, but it was a first run on soft ground over a shorter trip, and stepping forward markedly from that experience is a reasonable expectation. Her profile makes her a live threat; the main risk is rivals with more experience behind them.

runners_data.name: Ippy
runners_data.comment: A Kodi Bear filly on debut, hooded, with pedigree pointing to today's trip and beyond — a half-sister to Lady Of Inishfree, smart at a mile, and the dam very useful at a mile and a half. First-time-out uncertainty limits confidence.

runners_data.name: Lucy's Promise
runners_data.comment: Beaten decisively on her only start in an auction race at Fairyhouse, and a significant step forward is required to figure here. The hood applied for the first time is about the only positive angle, with the trainer out of form and her ranking bottom of our figures for this field.

runners_data.name: Violet Be Humble
runners_data.comment: A Cotai Glory filly on debut, with her dam placed at six furlongs at two, giving the family a short-side bias. There is little to go on without a run behind her and she is hard to recommend at face value; needs the market to say otherwise.

runners_data.name: Caoch The Piper
runners_data.comment: Trailing throughout when out of the picture in an auction race at Down Royal most recently, and has failed to make an impression in her last two starts. Pedigree suggests the step up to around a mile could help, but significant improvement is needed to feature here.

runners_data.name: Party In Vegas
runners_data.comment: A 35,000gns Lucky Vega breeze-up purchase on debut, with her dam showing useful form at seven furlongs and the stable having landed two of the last five runnings of this race — a genuine angle. The only caveat is first-time-out uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Sister Nancy
runners_data.comment: Beaten thirteen lengths into fourth on her only start at Listowel, and now faces a step up of two furlongs in trip that may stretch her further. The experience of that debut outing is useful but there is plenty to prove on both counts.

runners_data.name: Cashel Queen
runners_data.comment: Shaped promisingly on debut at Leopardstown when third, beaten five lengths on soft ground over 7f, with the step up to a mile expected to bring out more from her. She handles the conditions and stands as the clear top-rated runner in this field.

runners_data.name: Celtic Moon
runners_data.comment: Showed inexperience on her Leopardstown debut when fourth, beaten just over five lengths on soft, but enough ability was on show to mark her as a genuine danger. The mile trip looks to suit and her trainer is in form; the risk is the selection may confirm the form.

races.name: Champion Lettings Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Wicklow Gap
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Gavin Carroll and Gavin Cromwell with a poor recent run sequence (four figures 12-4-9-9) and a fade tendency; the step back to a mile is a slight positive but sim-going returns show zero wins and zero places on comparable ground, and a 28-day break offers little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Made no impression from rear in a Leopardstown handicap most recently, but steps down in grade here and that is the key angle. Effective over six and seven furlongs on a sound surface, with the tongue-tie applied for the first time; the main caveat is he may be stretched by today's mile.

runners_data.name: Nosmokewithoutfire
runners_data.note: Trainer T G McCourt has zero runners in the past 14 days suggesting no particular stable form, and this 3yo shows consistent tailender finishes (10th, 7th, 16th on stayertypes trips) — the drop to a mile is a logical move but one placing in three similar-ground runs makes the case weak; natural hold-up style will leave it deepest in a bunched field.
runners_data.comment: Trailing at the back throughout in a Dundalk maiden on his latest outing, he has shown little to recommend him across recent starts. The sire's record at longer trips at least suggests today's mile should be within his reach, but a big step forward is needed to figure.

runners_data.name: Dream Legend
runners_data.note: Ran well to win last time at 8f on Soft (1/9 on sim-going suggests it was a genuinely relevant prep) and the return to a mile on Good is a minor query; ED Delany stable is low-volume with one recent winner in 7 days, and the 71-day absence is the key risk factor, but a hold-up style that fades suits only if gaps emerge.
runners_data.comment: Third on his most recent start, beaten just over three lengths off a 57 mark and arriving just 1lb lower today with a win on the board over today's trip on similar going. He shapes as the one to beat in this field.

runners_data.name: Enthusiastically
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer who won over 7f on Firm for Sean Hayes and placed twice more over 7f — the step to a mile on Good is a question given headgear (hood/blinkers) and its best form came on Standard; Chris Hayes takes the ride which is an upgrade, and the form string (1-4-4-4) shows consistency without a recent win.
runners_data.comment: Outpaced at six furlongs at the Curragh most recently, but she has a win on the board and is most effective over seven and eight furlongs — today's mile sits squarely in her range. The first-time hood and blinkers signal connections are looking for a sharper effort; the trip increase is the key.

runners_data.name: Fontaine Khaled
runners_data.note: Jessica O'Gorman takes the 7lb claim on this horse whose best recent effort was 3rd at 7f on Good — four of five runs have been at 6-7f suggesting a mile may stretch stamina; one place on seven similar-ground attempts hints at limited upside, and a fade tendency tagged in the profile is consistent with that picture.
runners_data.comment: Third, beaten three and a half lengths off her current mark at Down Royal last time, and she looks capable of building on that effort here. Acts on yielding and good ground and is effective at today's trip; the wide draw from stall 15 is the one risk.

runners_data.name: Caoilte
runners_data.note: David Marnane has been in form (4 from 15 over 14 days) and this horse is a genuine hold-up type forced into a midfield map slot by the overcrowded rear — the sim-going record (1 from 6 on Good) is modest but a 35-day break is not alarming; discounted by the STYLE_FIT tag, it will need to fight for a position it wouldn't naturally seek.
runners_data.comment: Showed little at Fairyhouse on his most recent outing, finishing down the field, and a bounce back in form is needed. Effective over seven and eight furlongs and handles all-weather; blinkers applied for the first time may help him find more on the day.

runners_data.name: Due In June
runners_data.note: Colin Keane, one of Ireland's leading jockeys, takes this mount for Ian Donoghue who has had 2 from 16 recently — a natural hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to field congestion, but Keane's positional awareness gives it the best chance of any redistributed runner to actually secure a prominent spot; all four career runs on Good going (sim-going 4/4) is the most consistent surface record in the field.
runners_data.comment: Out of her depth at six furlongs in a Fairyhouse handicap last time, beaten eight and a half lengths, but the step back up to a mile today is more in her range. A jockey with a strong record at this venue takes the ride, which is a genuine plus; the form figures suggest more is needed.

runners_data.name: Hugo Spritz
runners_data.note: Recent run of 9th just 13 days ago and a career form line of 0-0-9 offers almost nothing to work with — a natural hold-up type pushed into midfield, and the short turnaround combined with a p-headgear note and poor sim-going returns (1 from 3) make this one of the most vulnerable runners in the race.
runners_data.comment: Trailed at the back in a Limerick maiden most recently with little to show across recent runs. Wears cheekpieces for the first time here and the switch to handicap company may suit in time, but the trainer is without a result from the last 25 and there is plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Stonyfalls
runners_data.note: Ran 9th on Soft and 6th on Good recently for Paul Traynor, with a 13-day turnaround and a fade tendency noted — its midfield placement on the map is a redistribution of its true rear-of-field style, and the sim-going record of 4 from 6 on similar surfaces provides modest grounding; needs better form than it has shown.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten, almost ten lengths adrift at Down Royal last time, and there is ground to make up on that performance. Acts on soft and has experience at today's trip; needs to show more than she has in recent starts to be a factor.

runners_data.name: Borora Aura
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner for Michael Mulvany (2 from 17 over 14 days) with apprentice Terry Casey claiming 7lbs — best recent effort was a 3rd at 10f on Good which shows it can handle the going, and dropping to a mile should suit its front-running style; the tactical advantage of leading uncontested at a moderate pace is real, though sim-going returns (3 from 5) are modest.
runners_data.comment: Beaten over seven lengths at Leopardstown on her most recent start, another below-par effort in a troubled recent spell, and a significant bounce back is required. Tongue-tie applied for the first time; handles the trip and conditions, but whether the gear change sparks improvement is the key question.

runners_data.name: Bullet Bourbon
runners_data.note: Showed a 2nd-place effort at 6f on Standard for T G McCourt but that form was on a very different surface configuration; a 34-day break, fade tendency, and the displacement from its natural hold-up berth into midfield all reduce its likely influence — the sim-going record of 0 from 13 on comparable ground is a significant negative.
runners_data.comment: In trouble in running at Down Royal most recently and beaten well, though that effort may be worth discounting given the incident in the race. Her mark continues to fall and she acts with cut in the ground over today's trip; the wide draw from stall 13 will need managing.

runners_data.name: Beau Army
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness has 1 from 27 runners in the past 14 days which is poor strike rate context; this horse showed two placings (4th, 2nd) in its recent form but both were on Standard going, and its true hold-up style, mapped to midfield due to field pressure, means it must overcome positional challenges — the 22-day break is fine but the trainer form is not.
runners_data.comment: Placed earlier in the campaign and effective over today's trip on good ground, she returns to a mark from which she has previously shown her best, with the stable having landed this race last year. The trainer's current run of results is the main risk to weigh.

runners_data.name: Cause I Like You
runners_data.note: Mulvany runner (same yard as Borora Aura) with Wesley Joyce claiming 3lbs — a hold-up horse whose best efforts over 8-10f on Good (three top-six placings) suggest a mile is the short end of its comfort zone; mapped to midfield rather than its natural rear position, the jockey claim is an asset but the sim-going record of 3 from 12 on Good is uninspiring.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in recent starts without threatening the frame, and the step back from ten furlongs to a mile today is expected to suit her. Wears first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces; acts on a range of surfaces and her trip range comfortably covers today's distance.

runners_data.name: Threebiggulps
runners_data.note: A horse with four consecutive finishing positions of 9-9-17-10 and a fade tag — J G Coogan has just one runner in 14 days and this 3yo's true hold-up style is squeezed into midfield by field congestion; the p-headgear is noted but the overall evidence points firmly away from a competitive effort over a mile on Good.
runners_data.comment: Outpaced and beaten down the field at Gowran Park last time when nine furlongs appeared beyond him, and he has plenty to prove. Wears cheekpieces for the first time here; the return to a mile at least addresses the stamina question, but improvement is needed to feature.

runners_data.name: Wedding Year
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness second string here (alongside Beau Army) with Rory Cleary riding — a hold-up type with a tp-headgear note whose best recent result was 3rd at 8f on Standard; mapped to midfield rather than its natural position, and the 10-day turnaround combined with a fade tendency and inconsistent form (5-4-3-0-7) makes it a difficult proposition.
runners_data.comment: Beaten well over ten furlongs at Ballinrobe on her most recent run, a trip that appeared to stretch her, and the drop back to a mile here is more within her range. Wears cheekpieces for the first time; acts over seven and eight furlongs, though she has plenty to prove at this level.

runners_data.name: Sayonara
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan is a significant jockey booking for Andrew Slattery (4 from 36 recently) on a horse that has raced over 5-6f throughout its career — the step to a mile is a major stamina question and potentially the most significant trip concern in the field; redistributed from its natural prominent berth into midfield on the map, though Heffernan may push forward to secure closer to its natural position.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Naas on his most recent run when sent over five furlongs, a trip that appeared too sharp for him, and a significant improvement is needed here. He acts on all-weather and looks at home over six furlongs; the step back up in distance is the one angle in his favour.

races.paceDynamic: Borora Aura is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner mile handicap at Bellewstown and will lead from the outset on Good turf, setting a sustainable rather than pressured gallop with no rival capable of seriously challenging for the early lead. The pace is therefore likely to be measured and controlled, with Borora Aura able to dictate terms and potentially get an uncontested breather in the middle portion of the race. Behind the leader, a congested midfield will form comprising the bulk of the field — virtually all of whom are natural hold-up or prominent types — meaning the race will compress into a single mass chasing one leader, with limited room for genuine tactical manoeuvre. This race shape strongly favours runners who can travel prominently just off the slow-to-moderate pace and quicken from a close position entering the straight, rather than horses who need to close from the rear of a field that is itself tightly bunched; the field holds far more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the back, and those most likely to secure a genuinely prominent position just behind Borora Aura are Due In June, Sayonara and Caoilte, all of whom are natural prominent/hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Borora Aura Controls Solo
scenarios.trigger: If Borora Aura gets a comfortable uncontested lead and the pace is moderate enough that she stays competitive into the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Borora Aura gets a comfortable uncontested lead and the pace is moderate enough that she stays competitive into the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just honest enough to string out the field and a horse travelling prominently just off Borora Aura sweeps through entering the straight.
scenarios.body: If the pace is just honest enough to string out the field and a horse travelling prominently just off Borora Aura sweeps through entering the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Weaves Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses midfield into a wall of horses and one closer finds a fortunate gap to finish strongly.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses midfield into a wall of horses and one closer finds a fortunate gap to finish strongly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse — Leader Holds
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is so slow that the entire field arrives together and the front-runner's tactical advantage turning in proves decisive by default.
scenarios.body: If the gallop is so slow that the entire field arrives together and the front-runner's tactical advantage turning in proves decisive by default.

watchPoints.text: Borora Aura (Terry Casey) — watch whether the apprentice can control the tempo cleanly from the front; if the 7lb claimer gets competitive pressure in the first two furlongs from any of the field's misplaced prominent types, the race shape changes entirely.

Sayonara (Seamie Heffernan) — Heffernan rarely accepts a passive midfield role and may push forward aggressively from the gate to get near the lead, which would increase pressure on Borora Aura and sharpen the pace significantly; this is the single biggest shape-altering risk in the race.

Due In June (Colin Keane) — Keane's presence is an outlier in a field of claiming jockeys and he will likely exploit his positional awareness to sit prominently just off the leader, making this the horse most likely to convert a midfield map slot into a genuinely influential early position.

Traffic in the home straight — with 15 horses tracking one leader and all mapped to midfield, watch for severe crowding as the field fans out for the final furlong; horses drawn widest may benefit from cleaner runs while those trapped on the inner could face significant interference.

Trainer angle — Mulvany runs two horses (Borora Aura and Cause I Like You); if Cause I Like You is ridden to hunt down its stablemate in the straight, watch how Casey reacts on the front-running Borora Aura, as stable tactics could influence the finish in an unusual way.

races.name: Ploughman Bar And Grill Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Dynamic Force
runners_data.note: A 7-year-old hold-up type for T G McCourt, Colin Keane rides from OR 60; solid recent Good ground form with 11 wins/places from 15 similar-going runs but won none; needs late cover to pounce and 18-runner traffic risk is real.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but returns to 8f after finding 6f too sharp at Fairyhouse last time; competitively weighted on his official mark and partners a jockey with a strong record at this venue, acts on good ground.

runners_data.name: Wellwhatshappenin
runners_data.note: 104 days off the track is a significant flag for Eddie & Patrick Harty's 4-year-old; hold-up style on Good going is fine but the long absence and a tendency to fade in the finish make this a speculative runner despite a recent win form string showing a 1.
runners_data.comment: Showed solid form including a win at 7/8f before a 104-day break, then was well held at Dundalk on his comeback in a manner that suggested the run was needed; handles today's going and has more to offer if recapturing that earlier level.

runners_data.name: Carvalhal
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in this race and likely to lead from stall to straight; R P Burns has had no winners in seven runs over the past fortnight and the horse steps up slightly on its recent form, but controlling the pace here is a genuine positional advantage.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap at Limerick 13 days ago by 2l — his sharpest effort in a year — and was placed in second the run before; effective 7f-9f on soft and good, stall 1 gives him the rail advantage and he is the one to beat despite a 6lb rise.

runners_data.name: Rockbury Lad
runners_data.note: Jamie Powell takes the ride on this 7-year-old; two wins from 11 starts in his trainer's T14 window and a tongue-strap today — genuine hold-up runner who has placed at similar trips on soft and good, stays the mile well.
runners_data.comment: Ran with greater purpose at Leopardstown last time on quicker ground and operates well at 7-9f on a sound surface; first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces could sharpen his focus and the handicapper has given him an opening, though draw 18 is a stiff ask in this large field.

runners_data.name: Roman Harry
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for S M Duffy who returns after 59 days; hood fitted, three placed efforts from five runs in similar conditions, but finishing position has been modest and lacks the class to dominate from a dropped position in a large field.
runners_data.comment: Rates a solid 7/8f performer on good ground and has the figures to suggest he can go close, but his turf reappearance at the Curragh last time was laboured; first-time cheekpieces are a positive on his return from a short break, inconsistency the key reservation.

runners_data.name: Dinamine
runners_data.note: Wesley Joyce takes the 3lb claim aboard this 8-year-old prominent racer; 1 win and 5 places from 11 similar-going runs is a strong record and a previous win on Good at 8f is a tick — natural style suits sitting close to Carvalhal and striking.
runners_data.comment: His most recent effort at Leopardstown came on soft ground after a rapid back-to-back — he had competed just 24 hours earlier — and that run can easily be excused; effective at 7f/1m on a sounder surface and clearly capable of better, he is firmly in the mix.

runners_data.name: Captain Ciano
runners_data.note: A true hold-up type at heart despite being mapped to midfield here — this 4-year-old for T G McCourt has struggled badly in 10f company repeatedly and drops back to a mile which could help, though form figures of -50009 give little reason for confidence.
runners_data.comment: Form has been heading in the wrong direction with four unplaced or near-unplaced efforts in his last five starts, and draw 17 adds to the burden in this large field; has course experience at today's distance and going but faces a stiff task from his current trajectory.

runners_data.name: Secret Magician
runners_data.note: Martin Hassett's 7-year-old wears a hood and is a genuine hold-up horse repositioned towards midfield on the map given the weight of hold-up types in this field; has one placed effort on Good from five runs at this going, form has been modest.
runners_data.comment: Fourth in our ratings and a genuine threat; held his level at Leopardstown last time but failed to see out 9f and the return to 8f looks a natural fit; acts on any going, first-time blinkers a positive focus, though he is yet to score.

runners_data.name: Virgil Tibbs
runners_data.note: 239 days off the track is an enormous concern for John McConnell's 4-year-old, and the horse has a pattern of fading in the finish; hold-up style and a very long absence make this one to treat with extreme caution despite the good ground tick.
runners_data.comment: Absent for 239 days and his trainer has gone 0/27 in the past fortnight; failed to get into contention at Dundalk before that long break and is yet to win in recent outings, with form at 1m to his credit but plenty to prove on these combined indicators.

runners_data.name: Tortola
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's 4-year-old has not run for 139 days, carries a fades-in-finish flag, and is a hold-up type squeezed into midfield on the map — three placed efforts on similar trips in its history but the layoff and finishing pattern undermine its claims.
runners_data.comment: Returning from a 139-day absence and her Dundalk claimer run before that break was well off what she can show; most effective at 6/7f, so today's 8f looks a stretch, and her inconsistency leaves her with plenty to find against this field.

runners_data.name: Rampage
runners_data.note: A 7-year-old prominent type for T G McCourt wearing a tongue-strap and visor; Sadhbh Tormey claims 7lbs and that is meaningful weight relief — has placed in Good ground previously and a forward-moving style suits pressing Carvalhal in a steadily-run race.
runners_data.comment: Effective at 8/9f on today's going but has struggled badly in recent starts and was well held at Leopardstown last time; draw 16 is wide in a big field, and while his mark continues to ease, first-time tongue-tie and visor may help unlock something.

runners_data.name: Pinball Wizard
runners_data.note: John McConnell's 8-year-old wears a hood; a true hold-up runner placed into midfield given the field's profile — two places from nine Good-ground runs, has hit the frame at 8f on Good before but OR 50 limits ambition significantly.
runners_data.comment: Disappointing at Gowran Park last time and carries the added concern of a trainer who has gone 0/27 in recent weeks; effective at 7-10f on today's going, first-time cheekpieces offer some hope but more is needed than his current form has produced.

runners_data.name: Micasso
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan aboard a 2-year-old (listed as age 2 in data — likely a data anomaly for an 8f runner) for Donal Kinsella after a 261-day absence; hood and tongue-strap worn, hold-up type remapped into midfield — the layoff is a serious question mark.
runners_data.comment: Absent for 261 days and made no impression in his final run at Dundalk before that lengthy layoff; draw 14 is on the wide side and first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces represent a fresh approach, though a significant step forward is needed given the evidence.

runners_data.name: Plastic Paddy
runners_data.note: Tom McGuinness's 8-year-old returns after 202 days (36 jockey days) wearing a hood; fades in the finish, is a genuine hold-up type repositioned on the map, and his two recent turf runs at 8f on Soft suggest he needs easier ground than today's Good.
runners_data.comment: Last seen departing a claiming hurdle at Wexford and has something to prove returning to Flat action on turf; best flat form has come on the all-weather over 8-9f, so today's surface is a concern, and first-time cheekpieces are the only new positive on offer.

runners_data.name: Desert Of The Sea
runners_data.note: A 5-year-old for T G McCourt who has raced 14 days ago — active and fit; hood fitted and hold-up in style, remapped to midfield here, but has two 2nd-place finishes at this trip and distance combination which is a positive angle despite modest OR 40.
runners_data.comment: Showed his keenness at Leopardstown last time on a longer trip and failed to see it out, but today's drop back to 1m suits better; at his best on a sounder surface, first-time cheekpieces may help him settle, though he sits towards the foot of the ratings.

runners_data.name: Mullacash Buzz
runners_data.note: Thomas Dowling's 8-year-old returns after 52 days with a hood and tongue-strap; hold-up runner moved into midfield on the map — has placed on Good ground at similar distances but OR 40 and finishing form suggest a minor role at best.
runners_data.comment: Set out too fast in blinkers at Roscommon on his turf return last time and faded badly; better on the all-weather at 7/8f and draw 15 is inconvenient for one who likes to lead, with first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces offering the main new angle here.

runners_data.name: Shelbourne Flyer
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's 5-year-old (no listed jockey in data) returns 22 days later; a genuinely prominent/pace-pressing type who is unlikely to get that position in this heavy field — last showed a placed effort at OR 53 on Good and the track suits, but being pushed back is a real tactical cost.
runners_data.comment: Struggled to find his best on his turf return at Limerick last time, and typically operates best at 7f rather than today's extra furlong; that run may have put him sharper for this but he has ground to make up on our figures.

runners_data.name: Hastily
runners_data.note: Tom McGuinness's 7-year-old ran 20 days ago and carries a fades-in-finish flag; form figures of 09-000 are deeply uninspiring and the horse is a hold-up type squeezed into midfield — a horse that has finished last or close to it in recent starts and is hard to recommend.
runners_data.comment: Struggled badly at Gowran Park last time after missing the kick and is without a win in five recent starts; most effective at 5-7f so today's 8f trip looks a stretch, and with a wide draw and an unreliable profile, she has plenty to overcome.

races.paceDynamic: Carvalhal is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner 0-60 handicap over a mile at Bellewstown, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Nicola Burns can dictate a measured, uncontested gallop from the front. On Good ground over a flat mile, a single pace-setter setting a sustainable tempo creates a race that will not truly quicken until the home straight, meaning the early fractions will be controlled and the field will bunch behind. This shape strongly favours horses who can sit just off the pace in a prominent or close-midfield position — they avoid early crowding, save ground through the bend, and have enough fuel left to challenge when Carvalhal is challenged late. The field contains a heavy concentration of hold-up types, but several — Shelbourne Flyer, Secret Magician, Captain Ciano — are genuine prominent/pace-pressing horses who are unlikely to secure their natural position in this traffic, meaning those at the head of affairs behind Carvalhal will be a select few who grab the rails or move early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Carvalhal Dictates, Pressed Late
scenarios.trigger: If Carvalhal controls a steady pace and the race only truly ignites in the final two furlongs, allowing close-tracking horses to pounce.
scenarios.body: If Carvalhal controls a steady pace and the race only truly ignites in the final two furlongs, allowing close-tracking horses to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If the steady early gallop produces a very compressed, slowly-run contest and the field fans wide in the straight for a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: If the steady early gallop produces a very compressed, slowly-run contest and the field fans wide in the straight for a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge On Rail
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops with a strong rail bias and a prominent horse tracks the leader inside to produce a sustained run from two out.
scenarios.body: If the race develops with a strong rail bias and a prominent horse tracks the leader inside to produce a sustained run from two out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the overall pace is so modest that Carvalhal never truly comes off the bridle and the field fails to close the gap in the short Bellewstown straight.
scenarios.body: If the overall pace is so modest that Carvalhal never truly comes off the bridle and the field fails to close the gap in the short Bellewstown straight.

watchPoints.text: Carvalhal (Nicola Burns, 5lb claim) sets off alone in front — watch whether any horse attempts to challenge for the lead early, because if the pace stays completely uncontested the front-runner becomes a serious danger to hold on.

Shelbourne Flyer, Secret Magician and Captain Ciano are all genuine pace-pressing types who are likely to find themselves further back than ideal in an 18-runner field — watch how quickly they are pushed out from the gate and whether they find a clear run.

Dinamine (Wesley Joyce, 3lb claim) is the most prominent-running horse in the chasing pack with the best recent Good-ground form record — watch his early position as he is the most likely to sit directly behind Carvalhal on the inside.

With 18 runners at Bellewstown over a mile, early position on the rail through the first bend is likely to be fiercely contested — watch for crowding and interference in the first two furlongs that could compromise the finish of any hold-up type caught wide.

Dynamic Force is ridden by Colin Keane, the standout jockey booking in this race — watch whether Keane produces a well-timed challenge from the hold-up position, as his ability to find gaps in a big field could offset the horse's need for things to go right late.

runners_data.name: Razmataz
runners_data.comment: Slow away at Fairyhouse on his only outing and unable to land a blow throughout, but his trainer is in form and the shorter trip today could see him closer; lightly raced with scope to improve, though he has something to prove before posing a genuine threat.

runners_data.name: Grayrobin
runners_data.comment: Beaten a long way on his only run at Nottingham and sits at the foot of our figures; scope to improve with experience but needs a significant step forward to feature in this, and there is little in the form to suggest it is imminent.

runners_data.name: Bit Of A Buzz
runners_data.comment: Shows consistent form across all four starts and produced his expected level again at Down Royal last time over 5f, finishing fourth beaten 8l; acts on soft and good and gets another chance here — a genuine contender despite being yet to score.

runners_data.name: Hip Hop Chrissy
runners_data.comment: Displayed useful early pace on her debut, tracking prominent before keeping on for third in a maiden — a solid introduction from a strong yard; the drop to 5f looks tailored to her strengths, she acts on today's going, and is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Santo Parvenue
runners_data.comment: Finished fourth on both starts in auction races without threatening, and his Cork run matched his opening effort; capable at 5f and has been freshened by a break since, making him a fair each-way prospect in the context of this field.

runners_data.name: The Drambling Man
runners_data.comment: Struggled to land a blow at Listowel most recently — the race was run to suit front-runners — and has finished no better than sixth in two starts; has some pace in his breeding which could see him improve, but faces a stiff task on current form.

runners_data.name: Ballymackney
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on her only start in an auction race at Cork and a significant improvement is needed to feature here; there is scope as a lightly raced filly and she has been freshened by a break, but the debut evidence leaves plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Annie Batt
runners_data.comment: Unraced filly with strong 5f pedigree credentials — a half-sister to a very useful 5f performer out of a dam who excelled at the minimum as a juvenile; she may need the debut experience but as an Equiano filly she has the speed breeding to pose a threat.

runners_data.name: Eastern Queen
runners_data.comment: Unraced Kodi Bear filly with a half-sibling who has shown smart form at 5f — though her dam was effective at a longer trip; likely needs this debut for the experience and may be better watched until she has had a run under her belt.

races.name: Indaver Ireland Handicap

runners_data.name: Billie Be Quick
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Mrs Harrington with Shane Foley booked; best recent Going form is on Soft-or-Good and the 5f trip suits, but finishing position has been weak lately (8th, 5th, 11th in last three) so needs a strong pace to run into.
runners_data.comment: Shaped honestly in Listed company at Ayr last time and is in her comfort zone at 5f on today's going; first-time blinkers fitted and the mark has eased, though she is yet to score in her last five and consistency remains a question.

runners_data.name: Rosie Frith
runners_data.note: Keane takes over on this Patrick Magee-trained 3yo who has placed twice at the trip on Soft-of-Standard and is moving outside her comfort zone on Good; the lone front-runner in the field and the key pace-anchor, but stepping up from a 27-day break and her Going strike rate drops on faster ground.
runners_data.comment: Has won in recent starts but her 2026 evidence is hard to look past — inclined to be keen, she was well below her best at Epsom last time, beaten 7l; effective at 5/6f on a range of surfaces but needs to rediscover earlier form, and a jockey with a strong record at this venue takes the ride.

runners_data.name: Namiid
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's 3yo carries the p headgear and has a win and five placings from nine runs at 5f, including on Good — strong course profile and Ben Coen's booking adds confidence; naturally prominent and likely to track Rosie Frith cleanly into the straight without the positional squeeze that affects the redistributed types.
runners_data.comment: Consistent performer who was off the mark two runs back and followed up with a solid handicap debut last time, beaten just 2l in blinkers; his figures put him clear at the top here, effective at 5f on this going and switches to first-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Smoke Them Out
runners_data.note: Seven-pound claimer Sadhbh Tormey rides this McCourt-trained 4yo who has raced recently (6 days ago) and steps back from 6-7f; hold-up style suits a pace-honest race but Good ground is a step up in terms of surface, with all form coming on Heavy/Soft or Heavier.
runners_data.comment: Has won in recent starts and is effective at 5-7f on today's going, but was well held at the Curragh just six days ago and needs a swift turnaround in form; a bounce back is required and the quick reappearance adds to the doubt.

runners_data.name: Sporting Hero
runners_data.note: William Durkan's 6yo runs in a visor and owns a win at 5f on Good, but his Going strike rate over this trip is poor (2 from 15) and he's been off 37 days; his natural inclination is to race prominently, but with Rosie Frith and Namiid already in that queue he's likely to face a compromised position, tempering the value of his style.
runners_data.comment: Has two wins in his last six starts but was comprehensively held in 12th on his most recent outing off a 3lb higher mark; fitted with a first-time visor today, effective at 5/6f on this going, though the handicapper may have his measure now.

runners_data.name: Treasured Royal
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's 3yo ran just yesterday and arrives on compressed turnaround, with consistent placed efforts at 5-6f on Good; a genuine prominent-type by inclination but the field is already stacked with pace and she is likely to find herself racing further back than ideal, which limits her scenario range despite honest recent form.
runners_data.comment: Ran at Down Royal yesterday on ground that appeared on the soft side for her best, and a quicker surface today looks a more favourable proposition; effective up to 6f on good ground but the overnight turnaround and a cold trainer add question marks.

races.paceDynamic: Rosie Frith is the lone confirmed front-runner in this six-horse 5f contest and, with Colin Keane aboard, she will look to exploit that role from the gates and control tempo on Good ground at Bellewstown. The redistribution flag matters here: Sporting Hero and Treasured Royal are both genuine prominent types by nature but cannot both slot into their preferred position behind Rosie Frith, meaning at least one will either push forward and pressure the leader or be shuffled back against their instincts. That competition for early position risks a messy, contested early pace rather than a clean, sustainable gallop — creating a scenario where the race is run at genuine speed from the front. This shape favours hold-up horses with a sharp late burst, giving Billie Be Quick and Smoke Them Out a tactical window if the pace burns brightly enough up front. The field holds more prominent types than the race can naturally accommodate, with Rosie Frith best placed to secure the lead and Namiid most likely to slot into second on the fence, while Sporting Hero and Treasured Royal face an awkward compromise.

scenarios.title: Rosie Frith Controls Cleanly

scenarios.body: If Rosie Frith breaks well and Keane controls the tempo without serious early pressure, setting a fair but sustainable pace.

scenarios.trigger: If Sporting Hero or Treasured Royal push forward aggressively to dispute the lead with Rosie Frith, injecting genuine early fractions.
scenarios.body: If Sporting Hero or Treasured Royal push forward aggressively to dispute the lead with Rosie Frith, injecting genuine early fractions.

scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate Track
scenarios.trigger: If the Good ground rides fast and the entire field races handily, compressing the pack so no true hold-up run materialises.
scenarios.body: If the Good ground rides fast and the entire field races handily, compressing the pack so no true hold-up run materialises.

scenarios.body: If the pace collapses entirely after early jostling and a late finisher gets a dream run down the centre.

watchPoints.text: Sporting Hero and Treasured Royal both want to race prominently — watch the first furlong to see which, if either, actually challenges Rosie Frith for the lead, as that will define the pace shape for the entire race.
Smoke Them Out races for the second time in seven days on Good ground having run all best form on softer surfaces — monitor whether the switch in conditions blunts the finishing effort.

Rosie Frith is tagged with a style-fit discount and goes on ground faster than most of her form — if she fades in the final furlong having set a genuine pace, Namiid is positioned to capitalise immediately.

Billie Be Quick's last five runs show a pattern of finishing 8th to 11th when the race doesn't develop to suit; Shane Foley will need an honest gallop up front to have any chance of delivering a late run at this 5f trip.

Treasured Royal ran yesterday and the tight turnaround is worth flagging — watch for any signs of a flat-footed early break, which would compound the already awkward positional compromise she faces in this pace-heavy field.

races.name: McNallys Pharmacy Apprentice Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Kevin The Great
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Gavin Cromwell with 25 days' freshness; his best recent finishes came over 10-13f on good and soft, so the step up to 1m6½f is a live question, though his prominent-closing style could allow him to track the pace if the field strings out.
runners_data.comment: Beaten just over a length at Navan last time in his first start in a tongue-tie, covering 13f well; handles this ground and takes just a 1lb rise in the weights. Effective between 10-13f with cut or on good, he rates a genuine threat here.

runners_data.name: Desert Friend
runners_data.note: 10-year-old for P J F Murphy who won over 14f on soft last time and has placed form over 16f, but is now tackling good ground again over a longer trip and has been beaten well at this course recently; apprentice Conor Cusack takes off valuable weight but trainer is 0/7 in the past 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in his last six starts demonstrate ability but he currently sits 6lb above his most recent successful mark; trailed badly out of contention on his latest outing and now tries a first-time tongue-tie, dropping 1lb in the weights. Each-way prospects are modest.

runners_data.name: Jurality
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner and race-shaper; Paul Flynn's five-year-old has a strong record in this going band (11/15 sim-going runs in the frame) and won over 13f on good at this course — his ability to dictate an uncontested gallop over 1m6½f makes him the most influential horse in the race tactically, though he is technically racing slightly out of his deepest comfort role.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap by over two lengths at Navan last time, reverting to a shorter trip with clear authority; progressive through his last three starts and effective on this ground at 12-16f, he tops our ratings in this field. Trainer figures are subdued but the form profile is compelling.

runners_data.name: Mystic Rose
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Patrick Magee who wears a hood and has placed on good ground over 12-13f but has not threatened at this course and trainer is 0/6 over the past fortnight; distance appears fine but this sort rarely wins in a race likely to lack the strong pace that would suit.
runners_data.comment: Beaten just over five lengths at Navan last time when tried over 13f; handles this going and has more to offer at staying distances, where she remains relatively lightly tested. Tries a tongue-tie for the first time today and holds a place chance.

runners_data.name: Maxwell Smart
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with T G McCourt and Sadhbh Tormey in the saddle; has placed three times over 13-18f on good, including third over 18f at this meeting's distance range, making him one of the most distance-proven horses in the field to press the pace from close up.
runners_data.comment: Placed third over hurdles most recently, showing a useful level of form before reverting to the Flat; suited by cut at 10-14f and second on our ratings in this field. Yet to win in recent starts but holds solid each-way claims on his best form.

runners_data.name: Voice Of Northeast
runners_data.note: A true hold-up performer whose last three handicap runs came off the pace before fading; the data flags a pattern of weakening finishes, and being pushed into a midfield map position doesn't reflect how this horse actually races — expect it to settle well off Jurality but the ⚠ fade flag is a real concern over this demanding trip.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Leopardstown last time off this mark, beaten two and a half lengths in a decent effort; off 48 days now and fitted with a tongue-tie and cheekpieces for the first time. Ranked tenth on our figures and hard to fancy despite that brief encouragement.

runners_data.name: Numidia
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old for Peter Lawlor who wears a visor and is fresh off a 12-day turnaround; suited in theory by staying trips but the last five runs show a pattern of mid-division finishes without threatening, and while mapped in midfield the horse's natural inclination is to race from the rear — the style-fit discount applies here.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Down Royal on his latest start, failing to respond when asked; acts on this going up to 16f but looks more comfortable on an all-weather surface nowadays. Mark has been easing and he tries a first-time visor, though hard to be confident.

runners_data.name: Al What
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's four-year-old has placed fourth over 12f on soft and has some distance experience, but finishing-fade flags appear on multiple recent runs; as a genuine hold-up type slotted into midfield by default, its realistic racing position is likely further back than the map suggests, which limits appeal in a race where the pace is set to be controlled rather than truly strong.
runners_data.comment: Well held at Fairyhouse most recently, finishing down the field on a day she failed to run to her level; effective at 10-12f and acts on this going but has been below her best in recent starts. Rated eighth on our figures and hard to make a case for.

runners_data.name: Celestially
runners_data.note: Donnacha Aidan O'Brien's three-year-old wears a hood and has placed fourth twice in recent starts; hold-up in style with a fade flag, but at 3yo with 7lbs lighter relative weight and some evidence of ability on good ground at 12f, there's marginal upside if the trip proves within range — trainer has 2/12 in the past fortnight.
runners_data.comment: Beaten over eight lengths at Limerick last time having shown ability over shorter trips; steps up in distance today where she could find more, and her trainer is in good form. Cheekpieces applied and she rates a solid threat despite being yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Miners Cabin
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse whose recent form string of 60000 tells a clear story; Kevin Thomas Coleman's four-year-old has finished outside the top ten in four of its last five starts at trips of 10-16f on good, and being mapped to midfield overstates its likely position — limited tactical appeal in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Always held up and failing to get involved at Down Royal most recently; winless in recent outings and has yet to show the ability to feature in a race of this nature. Hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Velvet And Vine
runners_data.note: Miss Jennifer Anne Lynch's six-year-old wears a hood and has placed fourth over 12f on three occasions; a natural hold-up performer whose midfield placement on the map is a redistribution consequence — the horse will likely race towards the rear, and without a strong pace to chase down, that makes it difficult to win from.
runners_data.comment: Beaten at Down Royal most recently, possibly finding the trip beyond her; effective at 10-12f and today's distance looks a stretch for her stamina. Bottom-rated on our figures and hard to fancy, though first-time cheekpieces provide a small hook.

runners_data.name: Bang Po
runners_data.note: Liam McAteer's six-year-old has finished outside the top nine in four of its last five starts, with most recent experience coming over shorter trips of 8-13f; the fade flag and poor recent form make it hard to make a case here, and its true position in the field will be at the back rather than mid-division.
runners_data.comment: Beaten four lengths at Navan last time, an improvement on his most recent efforts; handles this going but stamina over today's distance is a question given he finds 13f on the stretch. Rated eleventh on our figures and hard to make a case for.

races.paceDynamic: Jurality is the only confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field over 1m6½f at Bellewstown, and with no genuine rival prepared to chase him hard from the gate, he is almost certain to dictate an uncontested, controlled gallop on good ground. The pace is therefore likely to be honest but not searingly fast — a single leader setting a sustainable rhythm over a staying trip, which keeps the race together until the straight and means the race is unlikely to be run to suit extreme hold-up tactics. Prominent and mid-division horses who can travel close enough to the tempo to pounce once Jurality's advantage is attacked in the final quarter-mile are best positioned, particularly Maxwell Smart, who has placed repeatedly over similar trips in this going, and Kevin The Great, who has placed form over 13f on good. The field is overwhelmingly hold-up in profile, but several of those runners — Voice Of Northeast, Numidia, Al What, Miners Cabin, Velvet And Vine, and Bang Po — are genuine rear-of-field types shown in midfield purely because the map cannot accommodate that many closers; Jurality and Maxwell Smart are the most likely to actually secure the prominent positions that shape this race, and this scenario structurally favours a prominent or tracking profile that can exploit the controlled tempo.

scenarios.body: If Jurality leads unchallenged and the pace remains steady enough that tracking horses can coast into contention from the home turn.

scenarios.body: If Jurality's hold on the lead is never seriously threatened and the field lacks the finishing pace to reel him in.

scenarios.title: Chaos And Hold-Up Shock
scenarios.trigger: If a faster-than-expected pace develops and a genuine hold-up horse arrives from further back than anticipated to win in a finish.
scenarios.body: If a faster-than-expected pace develops and a genuine hold-up horse arrives from further back than anticipated to win in a finish.

watchPoints.text: Jurality's early position is critical — if any other runner attempts to press him for the lead through the early stages, the entire pace dynamic shifts and hold-up horses gain a live chance.

Maxwell Smart's jockey Sadhbh Tormey has had a quiet recent 14-day strike rate (1/12); if the ride is passive or too conservative early, this horse may not get its natural position close enough to Jurality.

Voice Of Northeast and Al What both carry fade flags and have been bumped into midfield on the map — watch whether they drift back to their natural hold-up position in-running, as a compressed field on a flat track at this distance could leave them with no ground to make up.

At 1m6½f on a flat course with good ground, the home straight at Bellewstown is relatively short — horses that need a long stretch to build momentum are disadvantaged, so the prominent-tracking profile holds a tactical edge over pure closers in the final push.

Several apprentice riders in this race have low claim percentages (2lb/4lb/7lb); Rian Lane's 7lb claim on Voice Of Northeast is the most significant weight advantage but the horse's finishing patterns suggest the claim matters less than the running style on this occasion.

races.name: Seamus Mulvaney Bookmaker, Crockafotha (Q.R.) Race

runners_data.name: Lark In The Mornin
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with two wins from prominent position over similar 14f Good-ground trips in recent form (/311-0); Mr P W Mullins in the plate for powerful Joseph Patrick O'Brien yard is significant, and the 39-day break follows a good campaign — naturally suited to tracking a lone front-runner and pouncing.|
runners_data.comment: Landed this prize twelve months ago and backed it up with another success shortly after; a shade below his best on reappearance but returns to a course and distance he handles well. Top-rated on our figures and commands clear respect.

runners_data.name: The Mediator
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott-trained nine-year-old with a solid recent placing record (three thirds in last four); a genuine front-runner by nature, the field's depth of prominent types has pushed this horse into the mapped midfield, meaning it will likely race out of its preferred role — small yard 0/21 in 14 days tempers trainer confidence here.|
runners_data.comment: Three consecutive placed efforts highlight his consistency and his connections have a strong record in this event; effective at 12-16f and among the stronger profiles in this field. Trainer is out of form at present but first-time blinkers could sharpen his effort.

runners_data.name: Can Happen
runners_data.note: Highest official rating in the field at OR=120 alongside Intense Approach; tongue-tie fitted and a wide-margin winner over 16f Good ground in most recent outing, though the jump from a 37-day hurdles background and the shorter 14½f trip are worth monitoring — prominent style suits the likely race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Shaped well at Ballinrobe last time over hurdles, coming through as the leaders set a strong gallop; all to prove on his Flat debut today but has shown he handles sound ground well over 2m. Wears a tongue-tie for the first time.

runners_data.name: Intense Approach
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner and the key pace influence in this contest; headgear (hood/pacifier) worn, 112-day jumps break for John McConnell, and the move to a flat qualifying race at OR=120 suggests connections are targeting this trip fresh — if fitness holds, the ability to dictate from the front is a clear asset even with the STYLE_FIT caveat.|
runners_data.comment: Struggled at Cheltenham most recently in a novice handicap chase, failing to travel or settle; has shown ability over fences at up to 3m but faces his Flat debut returning from a break. First-time cheekpieces applied but plenty to prove in this sphere.

runners_data.name: Swelltime
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up operator for a small stable with no recent winners; a 320-day layoff before a 35-day jumps run signals fitness doubts, and the repeated fade in finish is a structural concern — Good ground at Bellewstown has been fine historically but this horse's profile screams vulnerable from the rear in a steadily run race.|
runners_data.comment: Below par over hurdles at Limerick last time but has shown effectiveness on the Flat over trips up to 14f; steps back to the level where his best form has been recorded and rates a danger on his optimal surface. Yet to win in recent starts but holds claims.

runners_data.name: Talking Tough
runners_data.note: Showed a hint of form (6th and 8th recently) but zero wins on Good and a finish-fade flag; by nature a hold-up or prominent horse, the redistribution to midfield is because genuine hold-up space is already occupied — racing out of role at OR=34 for a small yard that has just one winner from two in a fortnight.|
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Down Royal most recently, failing to run to his level; effective at 12f and suited by cut, but his form has been sliding. First-time cheekpieces added and rated last on our figures, he is hard to recommend.

runners_data.name: Weston
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile from Henry Rogers's yard, 94 days off the track, and a form string of 0300-5 that includes a recent fifth over an identical 14f trip; the one placing in similar going (3rd, 12f Good) came from a mid-division position, so any run requires a strong pace to close into — not reliably supplied here.|
runners_data.comment: Comfortably held at Navan last time but has proven form at 12-14f with cut in the ground; returns after 94 days away and would prefer softer conditions than today's, but holds each-way claims at these weights. Third on our figures and yet to win in recent starts.

races.paceDynamic: Intense Approach is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival disputing the lead, is set to bowl along at a sustainable, self-controlled tempo over this 1m4½f on Good ground at Bellewstown. Lark In The Mornin and Can Happen will press from prominent positions, creating a compact early order but not a truly pressured gallop. That controlled pace over a middle-distance on Good turf classically sets up the prominent-to-lead brigade, keeping the race together long enough that hold-up horses Swelltime, Weston, and Talking Tough will be hunting ground from too far back to land a decisive blow. The field holds more prominent types than the map can accommodate — The Mediator and Talking Tough are genuine prominent/hold-up horses shuffled rearward by the numbers, meaning Lark In The Mornin and Can Happen are the likeliest to actually lock onto the positions directly behind Intense Approach. The race shape unambiguously favours prominent and lead profiles: horses able to travel in the first three or four throughout will enjoy first run and be hardest to peg back in the straight.

scenarios.body: If the early gallop is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and leave a meaningful gap for a hold-up horse to close into.

scenarios.body: If prominent horses crowd each other early and the pace collapses into a crawl, gifting hold-up types a sprint finish.

watchPoints.text: Lark In The Mornin is the horse to watch throughout — if Mr P W Mullins slots it cleanly into second or third behind Intense Approach from the outset, it is positioned perfectly to strike turning for home and its recent 14f Good-ground form makes it the most dangerous challenger to the pace-setter.

Intense Approach's 112-day absence and hood equipment mean watch the betting and early market moves carefully — if it shows signs of fitness issues in the parade ring or drifts sharply in the market, the entire pace map collapses as the only confirmed front-runner.

Can Happen carries OR=120 with a tongue-tie and is dropping back from longer hurdles trips; watch how quickly Miss Georgie Benson (7lb claimer) gets it settled in the early stages — if it over-races or takes a fierce hold, its chance of lasting home over 14½f diminishes markedly.

The Mediator and Talking Tough are both racing out of their natural positions due to redistribution — if either manages to pinch a forward berth at the start before the gates open, their effective race shape changes and the pace map is disrupted sooner than expected.

Swelltime's long absence (320 days before a recent jumps run) and repeated finish-fade flag suggest it will drop away from two furlongs out — watch where it sits early as a guide to whether the pace is genuinely strong or merely steady.
